name: Merge Conflict Kraken
description: Something ancient surfaces in `feature/checkout`. It has many arms and all of them are `<<<<<<< HEAD`.

rubber_duck.text: You talk through every conflicting line, one by one. The Kraken sinks back into `main`, sated.

stack_overflow_bookmark.text: You search for the exact error out of habit. Nothing useful comes up, but scrolling helps a little.

failText: You resolve it by picking whichever side looks longer. Production disagrees with your choice.
ignoreText: You leave the conflict for tomorrow-you. Tomorrow-you is furious.

name: Legacy jQuery Reawakens
description: A `$` appears in a file that shouldn't have one. Then another. The console fills with familiar, ancient warnings.

it_works_on_my_machine_badge.text: You wrap it in a namespace and back away slowly. It goes still.

hotfix_script.text: You patch around it instead of removing it. It goes quiet. For now.

failText: It spreads to two more files before you can stop it.
ignoreText: You close the tab. The `$` spreads through three more files by morning.

name: 2FA Lockout
description: Your phone is at 2%. The code expires in 30 seconds. It is, of course, the worst possible moment.

laptop_charger.text: You plug in with seconds to spare and get the code through just in time.

failText: You're locked out for the rest of the sprint, refreshing a support ticket queue.
ignoreText: You give up on the login entirely and let the ticket queue eat the rest of the sprint.

name: The Friday 5PM Deploy Curse
description: Someone deployed on a Friday. At 5:03 PM. On purpose.

hotfix_script.text: You roll it back before anyone notices. Mostly.

git_stash.text: You stash your way out of the deploy queue and let Monday-you sort it out.

failText: You spend the weekend un-breaking production.
ignoreText: You mute the channel and go to bed. Production does not mute itself.

name: Off-By-One Error Eats a Day
description: The loop runs one too many times. Or one too few. It has already been six hours.

stack_overflow_bookmark.text: You find the exact answer, third reply down, from 2011. It still works.

the_one_working_unit_test.text: The test catches the symptom, not the cause. It ships, mostly working.

failText: You lose the whole day to it and ship a workaround instead of a fix.
ignoreText: You let it run one too many times and call it a feature.

name: Force-Pushed to Main
description: Someone force-pushed to `main`. The last few days of commits are... gone? Maybe? Nobody's sure.

git_stash.text: You had a stash from two days ago. Crisis averted. The team buys you coffee.

failText: Three days of history, gone. You start rewriting from memory.
ignoreText: You don't even try to recover it. The history stays gone. So does some trust.

name: Scope Creep Gremlin
description: It started as "just one small tweak." There are now fourteen tweaks. The gremlin is feeding.

signed_nda.text: You point to the signed scope in the contract. The gremlin hisses and shrinks back to size.

readme_nobody_wrote.text: You point at outdated docs that vaguely imply a boundary. It buys you a day.

failText: You say yes to "just one more thing" for the fifth time this week.
ignoreText: You say yes to everything. The gremlin doubles in size.

name: "Just Circling Back on This"
description: A Slack thread from three weeks ago rises from the dead. It has three new participants and no new information.

readme_nobody_wrote.text: You link the README nobody wrote. Technically, this is an answer. The thread goes quiet.

failText: You reply "looping in @here" and immediately regret it.
ignoreText: You leave it on read. It comes back with four more participants next week.

name: Standup That Would Not End
description: It is 47 minutes long. Someone is sharing their screen. Nobody knows why.

tabs_vs_spaces_allegiance.text: You reignite the tabs-vs-spaces debate. The meeting collapses in on itself and everyone leaves.

failText: You get your 90 seconds of update time back. Eventually.
ignoreText: You mute your mic and stare at the ceiling for the full 47 minutes.

name: The AWS Bill 10x'd Overnight
description: A dashboard nobody checks just turned very, very red. Someone left a loop running. It has been running for nine days.

stack_overflow_bookmark.text: The exact fix, third reply down, from 2014. You kill the runaway instance with seconds to spare on the billing cycle.

hotfix_script.text: You kill the runaway process by hand, crudely. It works. You never find out why it was running.

failText: You eat the bill. You will be thinking about this bill for the rest of the month.
ignoreText: You let the billing cycle close on its own. It closes very, very red.

name: The Intern Pushed Directly to Main
description: There was no branch. There was no PR. There was, briefly, no CI pipeline either.

the_one_working_unit_test.text: The one working unit test catches it before it ships. Nobody knows why that test still works. You thank it silently.

failText: It ships. You spend the afternoon writing a very calm Slack message.
ignoreText: You let it sit in prod. Someone else finds it first.

name: Critical CVE Alert
description: A dependency four levels deep in node_modules has a critical vulnerability. It was published nine minutes ago. Security is already asking questions.

hotfix_script.text: hotfix_FINAL_v2_ACTUALLY_FINAL.sh patches it in prod before the scan re-runs. You will never speak of this again.

failText: You open a ticket. The ticket opens a meeting. The meeting opens three more tickets.
ignoreText: You leave the ticket open. Security opens a meeting anyway. The meeting opens three more tickets.

name: Cookie Consent Banner Blocks the Demo
description: The banner will not go away. The client can see it. It is, somehow, the only thing anyone comments on.

it_works_on_my_machine_badge.text: You wave the badge, blame the client's ad blocker, and move the demo along.

failText: You spend ten minutes of the demo explaining GDPR.
ignoreText: You let the client keep clicking around it for the rest of the demo.

name: Cannot Reproduce the Bug
description: It happened once, in front of a client, and never again. The logs are clean. The client is not convinced it was ever fixed.

screen_recording_of_the_bug.text: You scrub to minute 43. There it is, in full, uncut. You finally know what you're looking for.

rubber_duck.text: You explain it out loud, twice. You don't find it, but you sound very confident when you close the ticket.

tabs_vs_spaces_allegiance.text: You insist, with real conviction, that it's a formatting issue. It is not. Nobody believes you again for a while.

failText: You can't reproduce it. You close the ticket with "works as intended" and hope.
ignoreText: You let the ticket rot at the bottom of the backlog. It resurfaces during the next demo.

name: Secrets Committed to a Public Repo
description: A `.env` file went into a commit six hours ago. It's a public repo. Somewhere, a bot is already scanning for exactly this.

hotfix_script.text: You rotate every key in the file and force-push a patch before the scan finishes. Close.

it_works_on_my_machine_badge.text: You claim it was a decoy file and hope nobody checks closely. Some of the keys were real.

failText: You rotate half the keys before you lose track of which ones. The other half stay live.
ignoreText: You figure it's probably fine. It was not, in fact, probably fine.

name: A Dependency Renamed Itself
description: A patch-version update silently renamed half its exports. Your build still passes. Your app does not.

stack_overflow_bookmark.text: Someone hit this exact rename two hours ago. The fix is a one-line import change.

hotfix_script.text: You pin the old version and promise yourself you'll deal with it properly later.

failText: You chase the renamed exports through the diff by hand and miss two of them.
ignoreText: You ship on top of it and let the errors surface in production.

name: The Onboarding Doc Is a Lie
description: The onboarding doc says setup takes five minutes. It has taken forty. Step 4 references a script that was deleted eighteen months ago.

readme_nobody_wrote.text: You write the missing step yourself while it's fresh. The next person owes you a coffee.

failText: You muscle through it undocumented and forget everything you had to do by tomorrow.
ignoreText: You leave step 4 broken for whoever's next. Statistically, that's also you.

name: A Meme War Breaks Out in #general
description: Someone posted a mildly wrong take in #general. Fourteen replies in, nobody remembers the original point.
failText: You wade in with a well-reasoned reply. The thread grows four more branches overnight.
ignoreText: You mute the channel. By morning, everyone's forgotten what started it.

name: The Client Hit Reply All
description: A client hit Reply All on an internal thread they were never supposed to see. Sixty people now have opinions about your invoice.

it_works_on_my_machine_badge.text: You weren't cc'd on the original thread, technically. You lean on that, hard.

signed_nda.text: You cite confidentiality and steer the thread back on topic. Half the room stays annoyed.

failText: You reply to explain the context. This is, somehow, worse.
ignoreText: You let it play out in the thread without you. It plays out badly, and everyone notices you weren't there.
